id_and_class.summary: F. H. Bradley holds that sentient experience is the sole reality. At its most basic, consciousness is ‘feeling’: an immediate, pre-relational whole in which differences are present but not yet split into subject and object, and from which self, body, nature and judgment are later abstracted. All finite centers of experience are partial appearances of one all-inclusive Absolute Experience.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Felt Unity Within the Absolute

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Experience is the ground matter of reality: to be real is to fall within sentience, and feeling, thought and volition are the only material of existence. Phenomenal consciousness is both the basic datum of Bradley's metaphysics and, transmuted and unified, the whole of what is real.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Body and soul are correlated appearances abstracted from one experiential whole, not two interacting substances. The mind-body problem looks insoluble only after both have been reified as independent things.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (experience is the sole reality; self, object and body are abstractions from it, not sources of it)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: The subject-object relation arises within experience; it is not its foundation. The actual subject is never fully available to itself as object, because the felt background always exceeds what reflection can isolate.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Qualities are not atomic units. Qualitative diversity is given within an undivided felt whole, and reflection later picks out color, sound, bodily feeling and the rest.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: One Absolute Experience; finite centers of experience as its partial appearances; feeling or immediate experience; appearances (objects, relations, bodies, selves) that are real but partial and internally unstable.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through immediate experience and through thought, which is indispensable for knowledge but falsifies when treated as ultimate, because judgment separates the ‘what’ of a thing from the ‘that’ of its existence.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Three levels: sub-relational feeling below, the relational, subject-object consciousness of ordinary thought in the middle, and the supra-relational Absolute above, which includes the distinctions of thought while overcoming their one-sidedness.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal experience, the unity of consciousness, judgment and thought, the self, and the mind-body problem.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: The regress argument against relations: if reality were independent terms joined by relations, further relations would be needed to tie the relations to their terms, without end. So unity is more basic than relation.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Consciousness begins as felt immediacy, becomes cognitive by idealizing, predicating and judging, and finds its completion in the Absolute, where finite experiences are harmonized.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Experience is the medium of all reality, not a private container belonging to anyone. Finite centers of experience are partial aspects of the one Absolute Experience.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: The apparent interaction of body and soul is a phenomenon within the Absolute, not an exchange between distinct substances.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: The experienced present is an internally differentiated whole, not sensory units plus a binding relation. Reflection's distinctions presuppose a field in which they are already together.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Self-representation cannot capture first-person consciousness completely, because every act of representing leaves an unobjectified subjective field behind it.
core_claims_and_evidence: Bradley argues that reality cannot be externally related terms, since connecting relations to terms generates an infinite regress.
Immediate experience is a felt whole prior to the distinction between subject and object.
Objects, relations, bodies and selves are appearances: real, but partial and contradictory when taken as ultimate.
This is not subjective idealism, because reality is not a product of any individual mind.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical: metaphysical and phenomenological argument, especially dialectical critique of relations.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The Absolute is invoked as the necessary completion of finite experience, yet its positive character can be described only by analogies drawn from the finite consciousness it is said to transcend.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Bradley offers no neural mechanism, no psychophysical laws and no account of conscious access; the theory is metaphysical, not scientific.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent as a monistic idealism in which both physical and psychical descriptions are abstractions from one experiential reality. It rejects reductive physicalism, dualism, epiphenomenalism and atomistic empiricism alike.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Every finite experience, including error and evil, is transmuted into harmony within the one Absolute Experience.
